0.long_answer: The protein known to accumulate in the brains of Alzheimer's disease patients and also found to build up in age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is amyloid beta. In Alzheimer's, amyloid beta forms extracellular plaques that are neurotoxic and contribute to cognitive decline. Similarly, in AMD, amyloid beta accumulates in drusen deposits in the retina, which is one of the reasons why AMD is sometimes referred to as the 'Alzheimer's of the eye'. This shared pathology indicates overlapping mechanisms in protein misfolding and deposition between the two diseases.
